Next year marks the 20th anniversary of the iPhone — and according to reports, Apple is actively developing an all-new design to mark the occasion. Many expect the new device to debut as the iPhone 19 Pro (or more likely the iPhone 20 to coincide with the anniversary), but I believe there's a strong reason it might not arrive in that form.

Rumour has it the 20th anniversary iPhone will fulfil Jony Ive's original vision of a "single slab of glass." The display stretches to the very edges, curves around the sides, and a fully glass body. The display is rumoured to measure up to 7 inches, slightly larger than the iPhone 17 Pro Max, presumably because the bezels have been eliminated. It might also mark the first time under-display Face ID and camera technology arrives on an iPhone, eliminating the Dynamic Island cutout in the process.

On paper, that sounds like a stunning phone. However, I'm not entirely convinced it will succeed the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro as widely expected.

The iPhone 17 Pro shift

In short, the iPhone 17 Pro is a major practical overhaul. An all-aluminium body for better thermals, while the device has also grown thicker. This marks the end of Pro iPhones as the most ostentatious, top-tier offering. In its place, we now have the iPhone Air — an incredibly thin, premium-feeling iPhone that also takes the all-glass and titanium design mantle.

Given that shift, I don't think Apple will return to making glass the primary material of a Pro iPhone, since it would sacrifice thermals. In the current iPhone lineup, Air represents the high-end flagship, while Pro is now the no-compromise performer.

Apple will release the iPhone Air 2 in early 2027 with a second camera lens. Beyond that, the future of the iPhone Air is unclear.

I could well be wrong, but it seems more likely that the iPhone lineup between autumn 2027 and spring 2028 will look like this — with the 20th anniversary iPhone replacing the iPhone Air slot:

  • iPhone 19 Pro / Pro Max
  • iPhone 20th anniversary edition (two sizes)
  • Second-generation iPhone Fold
  • iPhone 19 / iPhone 19e

That launch pattern would be more akin to what Apple did in 2017. That year, the iPhone 8 and 8 Plus were still new phones, but the iPhone X sat at the top of the lineup, designed for those who craved a flashy new design.

The bottom line

It's worth noting that the leaks aren't on my side — the consensus still expects the 20th anniversary iPhone to replace the iPhone Pro slot. That said, there's still well over a year until launch, so anything could change.

If it does end up replacing the Pro iPhones, perhaps Apple keeps the iPhone 18 Pro around for another generation. I find it hard to imagine Apple abandons its pro-first ethos quite so quickly.

Of course, the iPhone 20 is still well over a year away — so rumours may well be painting a more radical new device than will ultimately arrive. If the final design is slightly toned down, then the iPhone 20 replacing both Pro models remains plausible.

What do you make of the 20th anniversary iPhone rumours? Does it make sense for it to replace the existing iPhone Pro design? Let us know in the comments.
